rubrics.justification: Mostly consistent with a good-quality expanded blastocyst with visible compact ICM and cohesive TE, but it overstates certainty by calling it full-to-hatching/late blastocyst and adds speculative features not clearly visible.

Integrates age, BMI, endometriosis, prior biochemical pregnancy, semen quality, endometrial thickness, and oocyte maturity well, though it could better address the unusual day-4 transfer context and limits of morphology-based prognosis.

Reasoning is generally logical and internally consistent, with prognosis appropriately moderated by endometriosis and obesity; minor issues include some overconfident morphology interpretation and incomplete handling of the day-4 versus blastocyst grading nuance.

Recommendations are broadly aligned with IVF practice, especially support for single embryo transfer and recognition of morphology limits, though the discussion of Gardner grading on day 4 is somewhat imprecise and the truncated fresh-transfer comment reduces completeness.

Provides useful practical steps such as proceeding with SET, luteal support, and general peri-transfer advice, but future cycle planning is only partially developed and the recommendations are somewhat generic rather than highly case-specific.
